question: Does thermal-camera-specific person cropping reduce the scale/background domain gap and improve missing-primary fallback?

evidence.sampling: every twentieth canonical training row, no label-based sampling

data: training clips only; all source paths and users excluded from model inputs
model: ResNet18 ImageNet1K_V1; mean pooling over temporal segments; 40-class head; frozen BatchNorm running stats

training.augmentation: shared spatial crop 136..160 resized160, shared horizontal flip; temporal segment jitter
training.selection: fixed final epoch; held metrics computed once after training

comparison: canonical release predictions and current paired TV predictions, reported separately; baseline encoders have upstream target-label contamination, thermal member does not
deployment: seed2026 only; no seed selection or multi-seed ensemble; fp16 state loaded into fp32 model and bfloat16 compute
fallback: if neither visual nor skeleton has valid input AND thermal is valid, replace output with thermal logits; all other outputs bitwise unchanged
stopping_rule: No detector threshold, margin, crop mode, weight or epoch scan on held results. No test inference unless original gates and the extra gate pass.
authorization: 2026-09-10 user authorizes independent experiments and Kaggle confirmation when evidence supports the candidate; standard release remains intact.
single_change: Apply existing YOLO11n union crop in thermal coordinates before the original TSN; no temporal shift. Same 0.25 confidence, 1.4 margin, 0.35 min-side as original visual cropping; eight probe frames; full field on no detection.
control: thermal_fallback_v1; no change to classifier, training or fallback
extra_gate: sum paired fallback net gains vs TSN across all three seeds must be positive
